page.layout: One printed page on the scan, with running text in one column. The gutter is dark at the left of the text column. At the far left is the cut-off right edge of the facing page, which is not transcribed. The running head is at the top, the page number at the top right, and the gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.l: 71 Testimonium igitur ipsum in se con-
estantis de re testata) nihil habet artis aut
virtutis arguendi, sed fulciri debet argu-
tis in teste apparet. aliud majorem, aliud
runtur, ad testimonii ac testis veracita-
[?]um inter se disponi. Hæc igitur Dispo-
[?]ventorum, vel eo tendit ut judicium de
manat, quasi ex flore; vel ut memoria
[?]int retineri: hi enim tres actus ratio-[?]s
inere, quibus tres interni sensus infer-
& per se vel sua luce manifestum,

page.notes: The left edge of the facing page is cut off and mostly unreadable, so it is not transcribed. Letters at the binding edge of the text column are hidden and marked [?]. The first word of the page is cut by the gutter. The words "eum", "inventorum", "possint" and "nis" are conjectures from partial letters and are marked [?]. The printed "ffint" and "eftantis" are copied as printed.
